meaning: to grow; to grow up; (长得) to look, in appearance

senses.en: to grow (children, plants, hair): 长高 'grow taller', 长了一岁 'a year older'
长得 + description: to look (a certain way); 长得像 'to look like'

examples.en: Your son's gotten so tall!
examples.analysis: 长 'grow' + 这么高 'this tall' names the result of the growing. 都…了 here means 'already', showing surprise at how much he has grown. Read 长 as zhǎng; as cháng the same character is the adjective 'long'.

examples.zh: 你长得像爸爸还是像妈妈？
examples.en: Do you look like your dad or your mom?
examples.analysis: 长得 + description is about looks, not growth: 长得像 + person = 'to look like (someone)'. 还是 joins two options, 'A or B?', so the question needs no 吗 at the end.

examples.zh: 今天是我生日，我又长了一岁。
examples.en: It's my birthday today, so I'm another year older.
examples.analysis: 长 + 了 + 一岁 'grew by one year': the amount of growth comes after the verb and 了. 又 'again' presents it as one more birthday in the series. People say 又长了一岁 on birthdays and at New Year.

meaning: prefix before a surname: familiar address for someone your age or older

senses.en: 老 + surname: friendly, informal way to address a colleague or friend about your age or older (老王); for someone younger use 小 + surname
老 + number: birth order among siblings (老大 'the eldest', 老二 'the second')

examples.zh: 老王，你今天怎么没来上班？
examples.en: Lao Wang, how come you didn't come in to work today?
examples.analysis: 老 + 王 turns a surname into a name you call a colleague by. It signals familiarity, not that the person is elderly. 怎么没 + verb asks 'how come you didn't…?'; said lightly it sounds surprised rather than accusing, though a sharp tone can make it a reproach.

examples.en: Lao Li, let's have dinner together after work!
examples.analysis: 老李 opens the sentence as a call to the listener, the way colleagues and friends often address each other. 下班 'after work' sets the time, and 吧 turns 一起吃饭 'eat together' into a suggestion.

examples.en: He's older than me, so I call him Lao Liu.
examples.analysis: 叫 + person + name = 'call someone (by a name)'. The first clause gives the reason: 老 + surname suits a peer or someone older than you. For someone younger, people use 小 + surname (小刘); to a much older or senior person, a title such as 刘老师 is the more respectful choice.

related.en: 小 + surname: for someone younger (小王)

meaning: dog

senses.en: dog (a pet, or dogs in general)

measure.note: 一只狗; 条 (tiáo) is also used: 一条狗

examples.en: Do you have a dog at home?
examples.analysis: 狗 is the object of 有: 你家 'your home' + 有 + 狗. Chinese needs no word for 'a', and 狗 can mean one dog or several. 吗 at the end makes it a yes/no question.

examples.en: I'm a bit scared of dogs.
examples.analysis: 怕 'to be afraid of' takes 狗 directly as its object, with no word for 'of'. 狗 here means dogs in general. 有点儿 before 怕 tones it down to 'a bit'.

examples.zh: 这只狗真可爱！叫什么名字？
examples.en: This dog is so cute! What's its name?
examples.analysis: 这 + 只 + 狗: the measure word 只 (zhī) sits between 'this' and the noun. 叫什么名字 'what is (it) called' asks a dog's name just as you would ask a person's, with the subject left out.

meaning: but; however

senses.en: but; however: starts a clause that goes against what came before
at the start of a reply: 'but…', to object or raise a problem

examples.en: I'd like to go, but I don't have time.
examples.analysis: 可是 opens the second clause and turns against the first: 我想去 'I want to go', then 可是 + 没时间 'no time'. The subject 我 is not repeated after 可是, since both clauses share it.

examples.zh: 这件衣服很好看，可是太贵了。
examples.en: This top looks really nice, but it's too expensive.
examples.analysis: A typical shopping line: praise first, then 可是 + the problem. 太…了 'too…' states the objection. 但是 could replace 可是 here with much the same meaning.

examples.en: But you said yesterday it was OK!
examples.analysis: Here 可是 opens a whole reply, objecting to what the other person has just said. 说可以 'said it was OK' reports their earlier answer, and 啊 at the end adds feeling, so the line sounds like a protest.

meaning: head; (measure word) for cattle and pigs

senses.en: head (of a person or animal)
for large livestock: 一头牛 'a cow', 一头猪 'a pig'

measure.note: 比我高一个头 'a head taller than me'

examples.zh: 我头有点儿疼，今天想早一点儿回家。
examples.en: I've got a bit of a headache, so I'd like to go home a little early today.
examples.analysis: 我 + 头 + 疼 'my head hurts': the person, then the body part with no 的, then 疼. This is the usual way to report pain, so 'I have a headache' comes out as 'I, head hurts'. 有点儿 softens it to 'a bit'.

examples.zh: 你头还疼吗？好一点儿了吗？
examples.en: Does your head still hurt? Is it any better?
examples.analysis: 你 + 头 + 还 'still' + 疼 + 吗: the person, then the body part, then how it feels. The follow-up 好一点儿了吗 asks whether it has got 'a bit better', with 了 marking a change.

examples.en: Watch your head!
examples.analysis: A quick warning at a low door or a car roof: 小心 'be careful' + 碰头 'bump your head'. 头 is the object of 碰, with no 'your' because it is obvious whose head is meant. 小心 can also take just a noun that names the danger, as in 小心车 'watch out for cars'.

meaning: to stand; to be on one's feet

senses.en: to stand; to be standing (站着)
站起来: to stand up; 站在 + place: to stand at a place

examples.en: Please don't stand. Have a seat!
examples.analysis: 站 + 着 describes an ongoing state, 'standing'. 别…了 asks someone to stop doing it, and 快 + verb + 吧 urges them warmly: a typical host's line to a guest.

examples.zh: 我今天站了一天，太累了。
examples.en: I was on my feet all day today. I'm exhausted.
examples.analysis: 站 + 了 + 一天 'one day' says how long the standing lasted: the length of time comes after the verb. 太累了 gives the result; here 太…了 means 'so…, extremely…' (I'm exhausted), not 'too…'.

examples.en: Can you stand at the entrance and wait for me?
examples.analysis: 站在 + place = 'stand at (a place)': 在 comes right after the verb and introduces where. 等我 'wait for me' follows as the second action. 好吗 at the end turns the instruction into a polite request.

collocations.en: to stand at; to stand on

meaning: chance; opportunity

senses.en: a chance, an opportunity (to do something)
有机会: 'some time, when there's a chance' (a friendly, open-ended plan)

examples.zh: 有机会我们一起吃个饭吧！
examples.en: Let's have a meal together sometime!
examples.analysis: 有机会 'when there's a chance' opens the sentence like a time phrase, 'sometime'. It is often a friendly, open-ended suggestion rather than a fixed plan. 吃个饭 'have a meal' uses 个 to keep it casual.

examples.zh: 这是一个很好的机会，你去吧！
examples.en: This is a great opportunity. You should go!
examples.analysis: 机会 is the object of 是, with everything describing it placed before it: 一个 + 很好的 + 机会. 你去吧 'go ahead' then encourages the listener to take it.

examples.zh: 我一直没有机会去北京。
examples.en: I've never had the chance to go to Beijing.
examples.analysis: 机会 + verb phrase = 'a chance to do something': 机会 first, then 去北京. 一直没有 'all along not had' gives 'have never had (so far)', which leaves room for it to happen later.

related.en: 有时间 'to have time', next to 有机会 'to have a chance'

meaning: hello? (on the phone); hey! (to get attention)

senses.en: hello?: to open a phone call or check the line
hey!: to catch someone's attention; can sound rude as a way to address people

examples.en: Hello, is this Teacher Wang?
examples.analysis: 喂 opens the phone call before anything else. On the phone many speakers say it with a rising tone, wéi. 请问 'may I ask' + 是…吗 then checks who is on the line.

examples.en: Hello? Can you hear me?
examples.analysis: Here 喂 checks the line in the middle of a call. 听到 'to hear' takes 我说话 'me talking' as what is heard, and 能…吗 asks whether it is possible.

examples.en: Hey, you dropped your wallet!
examples.analysis: Face to face, 喂 grabs a stranger's attention when you don't know their name. In a hurry like this it is understandable but abrupt; 不好意思 first is gentler, and as a general way to address people 喂 can sound rude. 掉了 = 'has fallen'.

related.en: hello (face to face; on the phone it often follows 喂)

meaning: to seem; it looks like; to be like

senses.en: seem to; it looks like: marks what you say as an impression (外边好像下雨了)
to be like; as if (好像 + noun + 一样)

examples.en: Looks like it's raining outside.
examples.analysis: 好像 sits before the verb phrase 下雨了 and marks it as an impression, not a checked fact. 了 shows a new situation, 'it has started raining'.

examples.en: I feel like I've seen you somewhere before.
examples.analysis: 好像 hedges the whole claim. 哪儿 is not a question here: inside a statement it means 'somewhere'. 见过 = 'have seen (at some point)', with 过 marking past experience.

examples.zh: 你今天好像不太高兴，是不是累了？
examples.en: You don't seem very happy today. Are you tired?
examples.analysis: 好像 comes before the negative: 好像 + 不太高兴 'seem not very happy'. It makes the remark gentler than a flat 你不高兴. 是不是 + guess asks 'is it that…?', offering a reason.

related.en: to feel; to think (states an opinion)

meaning: to finish; to be used up; (after a verb) done

senses.en: after another verb: finish doing it (看完, 说完)
to be used up, run out (牛奶喝完了)
to end, be over (电影完了)

examples.en: Have you finished this book?
examples.analysis: 完 follows the verb 看 'read' and gives its result: the reading is finished. 这本书 'this book' comes first as the topic. To answer, people say 看完了 or 还没看完.

examples.en: Hang on, I'm not done talking.
examples.analysis: To say a result has not happened yet, Chinese uses 没: 还没 + 说完 'not finished speaking yet', with no 了. 等一下儿 'wait a moment' asks the other person to hold off.

examples.zh: 牛奶喝完了，明天再买吧。
examples.en: We're out of milk. Let's buy more tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 牛奶 is the topic, and 喝完了 says what happened to it: it has all been drunk. English says 'we're out of milk'; Chinese names the action that used it up. 明天再买 = 'buy (more) tomorrow': 再 puts the buying off until then.

related.en: after a verb: done and ready (做好)

meaning: pretty; beautiful; (of a performance) impressive

senses.en: good-looking, pretty (people, especially women and children; clothes, places)
done impressively: 写得很漂亮 'beautifully written'

examples.en: Your daughter is so pretty!
examples.analysis: 真 + 漂亮 is an exclamation, 'really pretty!'. The adjective is the predicate on its own, with no 是. A standard compliment for a girl; for a man, people usually say 帅 'handsome'.

examples.en: Do I look nice in this one?
examples.analysis: Literally 'I wear this one, pretty?': 我穿这件 is the topic and 漂亮吗 asks about it. 这件 'this one' leaves out 衣服 because both people can see the clothes.

examples.en: Your handwriting is beautiful.
examples.analysis: Here 漂亮 judges how something is done: 写 + 得 + 很漂亮 'writes beautifully'. 你的字 'your characters' is how Chinese says 'your handwriting'.

collocations.en: well done! (praise for a job done well)

related.en: good-looking; nice to look at (more general)

meaning: minute (as a length of time)

senses.en: minute, for durations: 五分钟 'five minutes'

examples.zh: 等我五分钟，我马上就到。
examples.en: Give me five minutes. I'll be right there.
examples.analysis: 五分钟 is a length of time, so it comes after the verb: 等我 + 五分钟 'wait for me five minutes'. 分钟 counts minutes of time; a clock time uses 分 instead: 三点十分 'ten past three'.

examples.zh: 从我家走路过去要二十分钟。
examples.en: From my place it's a twenty-minute walk.
examples.analysis: 要 + time = 'it takes (that long)': 走路过去 'walk over there' + 要 + 二十分钟. 分钟 is itself a measure word, so the number goes straight before it with no 个.

examples.zh: 火车还有十分钟就开了。
examples.en: The train leaves in ten minutes.
examples.analysis: 还有 + 十分钟 'there are still ten minutes' + 就…了 'then it will…': the pattern for 'in X minutes, something happens'. 开 'to set off' is used for trains, buses and cars.

collocations.en: a few minutes; how many minutes

related.en: minute on the clock (三点十分)

meaning: to pick up (a person); to meet; to answer (the phone)

senses.en: to pick up, go and meet someone (at the airport, at school)
to answer, take (a phone call): 接电话
to catch (something thrown)

examples.en: I'll pick you up at the airport tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 去 + place + 接 + person = 'go to (a place) to pick someone up': the two verbs come in the order things happen. 接 covers both 'meet' and 'pick up'; the opposite is 送 'see off, drop off'.

examples.en: Who's picking up the kids today?
examples.analysis: A daily question between parents: 谁 'who' is the subject, then 去接孩子 'go and pick up the kids'. 孩子 can mean one child or several; context decides.

examples.zh: 对不起，刚才在开会，没接你电话。
examples.en: Sorry, I was in a meeting just now and didn't answer your call.
examples.analysis: 接电话 = 'answer the phone'; here 你 slips in between, 接你电话 'answer your call', common in speech. 没接 says it did not happen, and 在开会 'was in a meeting' gives the reason.

related.en: to see off; to drop off

meaning: measure word for films, games, shows and exams

senses.en: for a showing, game or match: 一场电影, 一场球, 一场比赛
for an exam or a performance: 一场考试, 一场演出. (A spell of rain or illness, as in 一场雨, is a different reading, cháng, and is not covered here.)

examples.zh: 晚上我们去看一场电影吧！
examples.en: Let's go see a movie tonight!
examples.analysis: 一 + 场 + 电影: 场 counts a showing, one sitting in the cinema. 去看 'go and see' + 吧 makes it a suggestion. To count films as works, people often use 部 instead: 一部电影.

examples.en: Did you watch the game yesterday?
examples.analysis: 那 + 场 + 球 'that game': 球 'ball' stands for a ball game here, as in 看球 'watch a game'. The object comes first as the topic, then 你看了吗 'did you watch (it)?'.

examples.zh: 我下午还有一场考试，没时间去。
examples.en: I've still got an exam this afternoon, so I don't have time to go.
examples.analysis: 一场考试 'an exam': 场 counts each exam sitting. 还 + 有 'still have' points to something left on the schedule. 没时间去 'no time to go' gives the consequence, with no word needed for 'so'.

related.en: time, occurrence (counts how many times an action happens; 场 counts events such as a showing or a match)

meaning: to beg; to ask (someone) for a favor

senses.en: to beg, plead: 求你了 'please, I'm begging you'
求 + person: to ask someone for help or a favor, humbly
to seek, try to get (more formal)

examples.en: Please, I'm begging you, help me out!
examples.analysis: 求你了 is a set plea, 'I'm begging you', often half-joking between friends. 帮帮我 repeats the verb 帮, which makes the request sound lighter, and 吧 softens it further.

examples.en: Can I ask you a favor?
examples.analysis: 求 + person + 一件事 'one matter' = 'ask someone a favor'. 求 is humbler and stronger than 请: the speaker admits needing help. 能…吗 asks permission before the favor itself.

examples.en: Don't go asking him for help. I'll help you.
examples.analysis: 求 + person on its own = 'ask someone for help', with a sense of depending on them. 别去求他 'don't go and ask him' uses 去 before the verb for 'go and do'. 我帮你 offers the alternative.

related.en: to help; to do a favor

meaning: just; only a moment ago

senses.en: just; a short time ago: 刚 + verb (我刚到)
only just, barely: 刚够 'just enough'

examples.en: I just got here. Where are you?
examples.analysis: 刚 sits right before the verb 到 'arrive' and places it a moment ago: 'I just got here'. 刚 alone is enough to mark the time. 你在哪儿 'where are you' follows.

examples.en: Looking for Xiao Wang? He just left.
examples.analysis: 刚 + 走 'just left': he was here a moment ago. 你找小王？ is a question with no question word, carried by the rising voice alone. 小 + surname is a friendly name for a younger colleague.

examples.en: Are you new here?
examples.analysis: 是 + 刚来的 'one who just came' asks whether the person is new. 刚 still sits right before its verb 来, inside the 是…的 frame. A friendly opener for a new colleague.

related.en: just now; a time word that can go before the subject

meaning: to change; to become

senses.en: to change, become different (没变 'hasn't changed')
变 + adjective: to become (变冷 'get colder')

examples.en: You haven't changed a bit!
examples.analysis: 一点儿都没 + verb = 'not even a little': here 'haven't changed one bit'. 没 negates a change that did not happen. A warm line when meeting an old friend after a long time.

examples.zh: 天气变冷了，你多穿一点儿。
examples.en: It's turned cold. Put on an extra layer.
examples.analysis: 变 + adjective + 了 = 'has become…': 变冷了 'has turned cold', with 了 marking the new state. 多 + verb + 一点儿 'do a bit more of': 多穿一点儿 'wear a bit more'.

examples.en: Has the meeting time changed?
examples.analysis: Here 变 is the whole verb, 'to change', with 开会的时间 'the meeting time' as the subject. 了 + 吗 asks whether a change has happened.

meaning: to see; to meet (get to see someone)

senses.en: to see, meet (a person): 很高兴见到你
to get to see (a place or thing, often one you have wanted to see): 终于见到海了

examples.en: Nice to meet you!
examples.analysis: 很高兴 'very glad' + 见到你 'to see you': the cause of the gladness follows it. Said at a first meeting, and also on seeing someone again, like 'great to see you'.

examples.zh: 你今天见到王老师了吗？
examples.en: Did you see Teacher Wang today?
examples.analysis: 见到 is one word: 见 'see' + 到, which marks that the seeing actually happened. 了吗 asks whether it did. 王老师 puts the surname before the title.

examples.en: I haven't seen him in ages.
examples.analysis: 好久没 + verb + 了 = 'haven't … for a long time'. 没 negates 见到, and 了 at the end marks the gap as lasting up to now.

collocations.en: nice to meet you; good to see you
didn't see; didn't get to meet
finally got to see; finally met

related.en: to see (with the eyes; things or people)

meaning: as long as; provided that

senses.en: as long as: 只要 + condition, (就) + result

examples.en: As long as you like it, that's all that matters.
examples.analysis: 只要 + 你喜欢 gives the one condition, and 就好 'then it's fine' gives the result. A common line when giving a gift or letting someone choose.

examples.zh: 只要明天天气好，我们就去爬山。
examples.en: As long as the weather's good tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
examples.analysis: The full frame: 只要 + condition, subject + 就 + result. 就 comes after the subject 我们 and before the verb. 只要 says this one condition is enough.

examples.zh: 只要你给我打电话，我马上过来。
examples.en: Just give me a call and I'll come right over.
examples.analysis: Here the result clause has no 就; 马上 'right away' carries it, and speakers often leave 就 out like this. 只要 stresses how little is needed: one call is enough.

collocations.en: as long as you like it

related.en: if (any condition); 只要 says one condition is enough

meaning: measure word for portions, copies, jobs and gifts

senses.en: a portion or serving of food: 一份米饭
a copy of a newspaper or document: 一份报纸
for a job or a gift: 一份工作, 一份礼物

examples.en: One more serving of rice, please!
examples.analysis: In a restaurant, 来 + amount + dish = 'bring me…', a common way to order. 再 'once more' + 一份 'one portion'. 份 counts a serving as one unit, common on menus, set meals and takeaway; for rice in a bowl, 一碗米饭 is just as usual.

examples.en: He's found a new job.
examples.analysis: 一份 + 新工作 'a new job': 份 is the usual measure word for a job. 找到 'find' + 了 says the search succeeded.

examples.en: Is this today's paper?
examples.analysis: 这 + 份 + 报纸 'this (copy of the) newspaper'. 今天的 'today's' stands without a noun after it, because 报纸 is already clear. 是…吗 asks yes or no.
